name: Angelita Morillo

bio.statement: The City of Portland says Morillo was elected District 3 city councilor in November 2024 and began her term in January 2025.
bio.excerpt: Elected as City Councilor for District 3 in November 2024 and began their term of office in January 2025.

bio.statement: Morillo's City of Portland page describes her as a Paraguayan immigrant and Portlander who has experienced homelessness.
bio.excerpt: As a Paraguayan immigrant and Portlander who has experienced homelessness here

bio.statement: Morillo's voters' pamphlet statement lists a background as policy advocate at Partners for a Hunger-Free Oregon.
bio.excerpt: Policy Advocate, Partners for a Hunger-Free Oregon

bio.statement: Morillo's pamphlet statement lists Lincoln High School and Portland State University.
bio.excerpt: Lincoln High School, Portland State University

bio.statement: Morillo's pamphlet statement lists prior service on the Portland Rental Services Commission.

positions.statement: Morillo's voters' pamphlet statement says she supports tenant rights and expanded homeownership opportunities.
positions.excerpt: She supports tenant rights, and expanded homeownership opportunities.

positions.statement: Morillo's pamphlet statement says she will push to create shelters by and for unhoused people.
positions.excerpt: She’ll push to create shelters by and for unhoused people.

positions.statement: Morillo's pamphlet statement says she prioritizes investment in public transit, bike lanes and sidewalks.
positions.excerpt: Angelita prioritizes investments in public transit, bike lanes and sidewalks

positions.statement: Morillo's pamphlet statement cites fighting for a fair Moda Center deal for Portland.
positions.excerpt: Fighting for a fair Moda deal for Portland.

positions.statement: Morillo's pamphlet statement says she led oversight of oil companies.
Morillo's pamphlet statement says she supports public safety by defending the Community Board for Police Accountability.
positions.excerpt: Angelita supports public safety for all Portlanders by defending the Community Board for Police Accountability.

positions.statement: The Portland Mercury reports Morillo brought forward an ordinance banning algorithmic rental price-fixing software.
positions.excerpt: Morillo successfully brought forward an ordinance to ban algorithmic rental price-fixing software

positions.statement: OPB reports that if re-elected Morillo hopes to increase accountability in city police programs, shelter providers and the budget process.
positions.excerpt: If re-elected, she hopes to increase accountability in city police programs, shelter providers and the annual budget process.

positions.statement: In a Portland Tribune Q&A, Morillo says Portland needs to expand social housing to increase affordable housing.
positions.excerpt: We need to expand social housing so there is more affordable housing in Portland

collection_log.result: nothing relevant (council agendas; press results duplicate step 5)

collection_notes: Steps run identically for all 21 District 3 candidates: (1) county Military & Overseas Online Voters' Guide statement PDF (with the full and large-print county pamphlets tried where the statement PDF was a scan; the pamphlet's candidate index marks candidates who filed no statement) plus the City Auditor's AUD-120 candidate filing form linked from portland.gov's 2026 city candidates page; (2) portland.gov/council roster and councilor page for incumbents; (3) campaign domain only as printed in the pamphlet statement or filing form; (4) one general WebSearch; (5) three fixed allowed-domain WebSearch groups (opb.org+oregoncapitalchronicle.com+wweek.com+ballotpedia.org; kgw.com+koin.com+kptv.com+katu.com; portlandmercury.com+vote411.org+pamplinmedia.com+portlandtribune.com) because the search proxy rejects oregonlive.com and apnews.com; (6) the three articles that cover the whole District 3 field: OPB 'What to know about Portland's District 3 council race' (2026-10-07), Portland Mercury 'Meet the Candidates For City Council District 3' (2026-09-09) and Portland Tribune 'Meet the Portland City Council District 3 candidates' (2026-10-13; Q&A — the Tribune says Sollitt, Pham, Parker, McCormick, Kelly and Frankenstein did not respond and Tucker withdrew). Multi-winner race: OPB states three council seats are available in District 3. Excerpts come through a summarizing fetch tool that limits verbatim quotes to ~125 characters, so some are fragments. Ballot name/order match inventory.json and the county Ballot Content RCV report. Incumbent per portland.gov/council (listed under District 3).
